# DraCuLa StreamNZB Template 6.4.3 — release notes draft

<!-- Auto-generated draft, seeded verbatim from the CHANGELOG section below. Condense for public release-note tone before merging the release-preparation PR -- this is a review starting point, not final prose. -->

## Changes

### Fixed

- **vidhin:** sync `generated/streamnzb-defines.txt`/`generated/vidhin-defines.json` with current upstream `Vidhin05/Releases-Regex` (`Radarr Web T3`, `Sonarr Web T3`, `Radarr LQ Groups`, `Sonarr LQ Groups`), closing a real drift a 2026-09-23 audit found (see `backlog-roadmap.md`): `HHWEB` has been removed from upstream `Radarr Web T3`/`Sonarr Web T3` and no longer maps into DraCuLa's `Movies WEB T3 Groups`/`Shows WEB T3 Groups` Defines; `126811` was added to upstream's `Radarr/Sonarr LQ Groups` and now maps into `Movies LQ Groups`/`Shows LQ Groups`. This is release-driving, not a cosmetic content sync: `HHWEB` releases lose the `+100` `Movies WEB T3`/`Shows WEB T3` native tier score, and — more materially — lose their exemption from `Reject suspicious 4K upscale` (`profiles/rules.json`, unchanged), so a `2160p` `HHWEB` `WEB-DL` release with no other qualifying trust/fallback condition (no `2160p` remux/UHD-tier alternative present, not a Library result) is now rejected outright when a `1080p` remux alternative exists in the same result pool — real-engine-confirmed (see the new regression below). `126811` flows through the existing generic `Movies/Shows LQ Penalty` (`-10000`)/`Adaptive Low-Score Filtering` mechanism with no new rule, when supplied as the parsed release group. Real-engine verification found that pinned Jhin does not extract a trailing `-126811` token as a release group; `-A126811` was also not extracted, while a letter-suffixed `-126811A` group token was parsed successfully — an upstream parser characteristic, not a DraCuLa mapping defect, and not addressed here. No rule, scoring value, Best-N behavior, SeaDex behavior, `Reject suspicious 4K upscale`'s own predicate, or StreamNZB/Jhin pin changed; `profile.txt`/`profile-neutral.txt` are byte-for-byte unchanged (160/159 rules, Define-library-only content sync). `scripts/sync_vidhin.py`'s comment explaining why the separate, still-deferred conditional `LQ (Release Title) (Radarr)` HHWEB branch stays unconsumed is corrected — it previously cited HHWEB's now-obsolete WEB T3 trust-tier status as (part of) the reason; the still-valid reasons (no documented upstream rationale for the conditional Radarr-only classification, no equivalent Sonarr branch, no concrete failing-release evidence) are unchanged and the branch remains deliberately unconsumed, a separate, still-open policy question this PR does not resolve.
- **testing:** update the two now-stale `tests/golden_defines.json` anchor-token expectations for `Movies WEB T3 Groups` (`HHWEB` → `BLOOM`, a real, currently-live member) and `Shows WEB T3 Groups` (`HHWEB` dropped, `DRACULA`/`ViSiON` retained) so the guard continues to assert genuine current membership rather than a removed token — the assertion itself is presently dormant (only exercised against a historical schema-v1 baseline shape the committed baseline no longer carries), but the expectation data is corrected regardless rather than left stale.
- **testing:** add `tests/streamnzb_compat/hhweb_web_t3_sync_test.go`, 5 new real-engine regressions against the exact published production rules and the real, freshly-synced Define library: `HHWEB` no longer matches `Movies WEB T3 Groups`/`Shows WEB T3 Groups` (2 tests); a `2160p` `HHWEB` `WEB-DL` candidate with no qualifying trust/fallback is now rejected by `Reject suspicious 4K upscale`, scoring and surviving identically to a same-shape unclassified control (proving the change is driven purely by lost tier membership, not a group-specific carve-out); the rule's own `not library` exemption remains unaffected for an otherwise-identical Library `HHWEB` candidate; and a `1080p` `HHWEB` candidate is never rejected, proving the change is strictly mediated through the `2160p`-scoped upscale guard, not a blanket `HHWEB` rejection.
